page0.text:
It's been a few hours since I started training.
My sparring with Saber can't be likened to kendo.
To begin with, Saber isn't trained in kendo, and seems like she has no intention of teaching me swordplay.

page1.text:
No, what Saber is literally pounding into me is combat itself.
She's getting me used to fighting for my life so that I'll be able to maintain my composure and physical performance in a mortal battle against another Master.

page2.text:
This was Saber's idea, and I'm extremely grateful for the crash course.
I won't be able to improve my swordsmanship enough to matter in one or two days.
Shirou Emiya can only rely on the body he's trained until this day.
If I can gain enough experience to respond to a life-or-death situation, that'll be the surest weapon of all...

page3.text:
"I have you!"
"Ow!"
And, as you'd expect...
The instant I'm distracted by my thoughts, Saber nails me squarely in the chest with a thrust from her shinai.

page4.text:
"Shirou. You must not let your guard down just because you've retreated out of your opponent's reach.
Try to allow yourself to relax only when you're here at home."

page5.text:
"Argh... Sorry. I did drop my guard there."
I cough as I get up, rubbing the spot where she stabbed me.

page6.text:
"...Phew. You can be surprisingly perceptive at times, but I have also seen you act with reckless abandon. If you could just rein in that flaw..."
Suddenly, Saber looks away.

page7.text:
"What's wrong, Saber? Did something happen?"
"No. Sakura is waving from outside... She appears to be calling for you."
"For me...?"

page8.text:
...I wonder why.
Sakura was trying to stop our training because she couldn't bear to watch me get my butt kicked any longer.
When I turned her away, she went back to the living room looking bored...

page9.text:
"...I'm going to the living room for a bit. Is that all right, Saber?"
"We have been training for two hours, so let us take a break."
"Thanks. I'll make us some tea, too."

page10.text:
"Ah, Senpai."
I hurry to the living room and see Sakura standing in front of the telephone.

page11.text:
"...Um, there's a phone call. They've been waiting for a while. Here you go."
Sakura steps away from the phone.
"A phone call...? At this hour?"
Is it Fuji-nee...? I pick up the receiver, expecting her to ask me to bring her something she left at home.

page12.text:
"Let's see. Hello, I've just been handed the phone.
This is Emiya speaking—"

page13.text:
"THIS IS NO TIME FOR THAT!
WHO GAVE YOU PERMISSION TO
STAY HOME FROM SCHOOL!?"

page14.text:
The speaker roars in my ear.
Actually, there must be some crazy magecraft at work to make such a small speaker fill the room with her shouting.

page15.text:
"Aaaarrgh, that hurts..."
My ears ring and my head throbs.
"Hey, are you listening to me!? Are you actually okay, Emiya!?"

page16.text:
"...I hear you, so lower your voice a little. You're going to burst my eardrums if you do that again."
"...Hmph. I don't know if I should say that you never change, or that there's something wrong with you. Anyway, it sounds like you're fine.
Ugh, I can't believe I got so worried about you."

page18.text:
"Well, sorry about that. Anyway, what do you want?
Something must have happened for you to call all of a sudden."
"That's what I want to ask you. I gave you warning after warning, but you still went to Ryudou Temple yesterday."

page19.text:
"Urgh. How do you know that?"
"I had someone keep a lookout... Looks like nothing happened, though. I assumed you had a little mishap when you didn't show up at school."

page20.text:
"Haah. You mean you think I got myself killed?"
"Yeah. I thought they chopped you up into little pieces and buried you in the hills."
"..."
Um.
That's a lot worse than a "little mishap."

page21.text:
"I hate to disappoint you but I'm...not exactly fighting fit, but I'll manage.
So what do you want, Tohsaka?"
"Huh...? I just—"

page22.text:
"Enough digging for intel on each other.
Oh, you want to know about the Master at Ryudou Temple. They already got—no, they were gone by the time we got there.
They got betrayed by their own Servant. By Caster.
And then..."

page23.text:
...I shouldn't say any more.
I've been speaking in a low voice, but Sakura is still behind me.
I shouldn't mention anything shocking, like people dying.

page24.text:
"Anyway, there isn't a Master or Servant at Ryudou Temple anymore. That's what you wanted to ask, right?"
"...Y-yeah. Glad you figured it out."
"Then I'm hanging up. I'm in the middle of training, and I'm sore all over."
I end with a 'later,' and move to replace the receiver.

page25.text:
"H-hold it!"
"? What now? I thought we were done."
"W-we're not done yet! Look, just come to school tomorrow. I have something important to tell you."
Slam. Beep. Beep.
The caller violently hangs up. That's so Tohsaka.

page26.text:
"...Jeez. She's mad that I went yesterday, and now she's telling me to come. There's no pleasing her."
I return the phone receiver to its base.
I turn around to go back to the living room and finish making tea.

page27.text:
But...
Sakura is in my way.

page28.text:
"Sakura? What's wrong? Are you not feeling well?"
"No, I don't have a fever. It's just...you looked so happy, so I was wondering why."

page29.text:
"Huh?"
Me? Happy?
Is she saying I was happy that Tohsaka called me?

page30.text:
"No way. I'm mad, actually."
"...You didn't notice, then."
Sakura awkwardly avoids meeting my eyes.

page31.text:
"...Hm."
I'm still confused, but I take the chance to finish making tea for three.

page32.text: By the time training is over, everything outside is suffused in dark red light.

page33.text:
"Senpai, I'm done prepping the amberjack. That just leaves the tomatoes and pumpkin, right?"
"Yeah, I took care of those. Next, we'll season the sauce and grill them once that's done... Oh, and I'm going to steam the egg custard, so get the big bowls. Fuji-nee splurged and bought crab yesterday, for some reason."

page34.text:
"Oh, you're adding crab-flavored fish cake! I love the way they look and taste."
With a huff of exertion, Sakura sets the bowls down on the kitchen counter.
I put my heart into making dinner as thanks for everyone's help during breakfast and lunch.

page35.text: I'd prefer it if Sakura relaxed in the living room like Saber, but she's stubborn about helping as she always does.

page36.text:
"Hm?"
In the middle of the dinner hustle,
the doorbell rings.
Sakura's here next to me, so it must be a visitor.

page37.text:
"I'll go get it. If they're selling newspapers, I'll turn them down."
"Sakura?"
Sakura goes to the house entrance before I can stop her.

page38.text:
...
...Something is making me anxious.
I put down the daikon I've been peeling and go to check on the front door.

page39.text:
Whoever it is keeps ringing the doorbell.
The nonstop ding-donging sounds almost manic.
Sakura lets the visitor know she's coming, and unlocks the door.

page40.text:
An instant later,
"It's time to come home, Sakura."
I hear a smooth, melodramatic voice. It clashes with the rude way its owner shoves his way into the house.

page41.text:
It all happened in a second.
The doorbell rang nonstop.
"Hello, may I help you?"
Sakura unlocked the door.
"Ngh!"
Shinji wrenched the door open and stepped inside.

page42.text:
"My broth—!?"
"It's time to come home, Sakura."
Without missing a beat, Shinji grabs Sakura's arm,
and drags her toward the door, ignoring her dismay.

page43.text:
"Wha—"
I run.
By the time I get there, Shinji's already one foot out the door.

page44.text:
"What do you think you're doing, Shinji!?"
"Hey, Emiya. I'm here to take my little sister home. Something wrong with that?"
"You're taking her home?"

page45.text:
"Hey, now. There's nothing wrong with me coming to pick up my little sister.
If anything, you're the one who tempted her to come over. I hope you weren't planning to use her against me."

page46.text:
...
I don't know what to say.
Did Shinji just...

page47.text: "Or, what? Were you planning to use my sister as a shield while you sneak around? That's pretty cowardly of you."

page49.text:
"What are you looking at me like that for? Are you stupid?"
"Shinji."
"Ha! There it is! Let's pick up where we left off, Emiya!"

page50.text:
My hands ball into fists.
I can't keep my cool.
I...
